statement.p: Calculate the total mass of a circular piece of wire of radius 2 cm centered at the origin whose mass density is \rho(x,y)=x^2~\mathrm{g/cm}.

static.solution: M=\int_{\mathcal{C}} x^2 \,ds We use the following parametrization of the wire: \mathbf{c}(t)=( 2 \cos t, 2 \sin t ),\quad 0\le t\le 2\pi Hence, {\mathbf{c}}'(t)= \left\lt -2 \sin t,\,2 \cos t \right> \quad\Rightarrow\quad \| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| =\sqrt{{( -2 \sin t )}^2+{( 2 \cos t )}^2}=2 We compute the line integral using the Theorem on Scalar Line Integrals. We get M = \int_0^{2\pi } \rho \left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| \,dt= \int_0^{2\pi } {( 2 \cos t )}^2\cdot 2 \,dt= 8\int_0^{2\pi } \cos^2t \,dt=8\left(\frac{t}{2}+\frac{\sin 2t}{4}\right)\bigg|_0^{2\pi }=8\cdot \frac{2\pi }{2}=8\pi \mathrm{g}
